&amp; ?<hr><font size="1"><span style="font-size: 12px;">C rule: If a function needs to <b>modify</b> your<br>variable, you must pass its <b>address</b>.<br><br>Without &amp;: function gets a stars?<hr><font size="1"><span style="font-size: 12px;"><font face="Courier New">A_d</font> is already a <font face="Courier New">float*</font> (one star)<br><br>The <b>address of</b> a <font face="Courier New">float*</font> is a <font face="Courier New">float**</font><br><br>Like: if a book is <i>one level</i>,<br>the shelf holding the book is <i>two levels</i><br><br><font face="Courier New">float x;</font> → value<br><font face="Courier New">float *p;</font> → pointer to value<br><font face="Courier New">float **pp;</font> → pointer to pointer</span></font>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry cast?<hr><font size="1"><span style="font-size: 12px;">cudaMalloc is <b>generic</b> — it works with<br>any type (float, int, char, struct...)<br><br>So it expects <font face="Courier New">void**</font> (generic pointer)<br><br>Your <font face="Courier New">&amp;A_d</font> is <font face="Courier New">float**</font> specifically<br>The cast says: &quot;treat this as generic&quot;<br><br>It's a <i>type-safety promise</i> to the compiler.<br>No data is changed — just the label.</span></font>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="195" width="310" x="950" y="550" New">cudaMalloc(A_d, size)</font> ← WRONG!<br><br>cudaMalloc would get the <b>current value</b> of A_d (which is garbage)<br>It would allocate GPU memory... but have no way to tell YOU the address!<br>Your A_d would still be ??? after the call.<br><br>It's like telling a delivery person your old address<br>instead of giving them your mailbox key." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" div.div:
&A_d — Why the & ?C rule: If a function needs to modify your
variable, you must pass its address.
Without &: function gets a COPY
→ changes the copy, your original unchanged
With &: function gets the LOCATION
→ writes directly into your variable ✓

div.div:
** — Why two stars?A_d is already a float* (one star)
The address of a float* is a float**
Like: if a book is one level,
the shelf holding the book is two levels
float x; → value
float *p; → pointer to value
float **pp; → pointer to pointer

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 288px; height: 1px; padding-top: 545px; margin-left: 922px;

div.div:
(void**) — Why the cast?cudaMalloc is generic — it works with
any type (float, int, char, struct...)
So it expects void** (generic pointer)
Your &A_d is float** specifically
The cast says: "treat this as generic"
It's a type-safety promise to the compiler.
No data is changed — just the label.

div.div:
If you wrote: cudaMalloc(A_d, size) ← WRONG!
cudaMalloc would get the current value of A_d (which is garbage)
It would allocate GPU memory... but have no way to tell YOU the address!
Your A_d would still be ??? after the call.
It's like telling a delivery person your old address
instead of giving them your mailbox key.

↑ ↑ ↑
| | |
cast to address how many
generic of your bytes to
type pointer allocate
"I don't care "WHERE to "HOW MUCH
what type" write the to reserve
result" on GPU"
